1.explanation_en: 即 means to take up or assume, and 位 refers to a position or office; together they form a conventional expression for taking the throne.
被 marks the subject as undergoing an action, and 害 is the verb “harm”; together they form a passive construction, with no agent stated here.
惊 means “be startled”; 倒 is a result complement indicating that the startling is followed by falling over.
不见 literally means “not be seen”; here it describes the snake becoming absent. The attached 了 marks the change of state.
夹 is the verb “be mixed with”; 着 marks this continuing state.
卷 describes the sweeping action, and 走 is a resultative complement showing that something is carried away.
带 is the verb “carry/bring”; attached 着 marks the accompanying state of having something with him.
作 means “serve as,” and 内应 names the role of an agent who assists from within. Together they form a compact role expression.
关 means “confine”; 进 is a directional complement showing movement into a place, and 牢里 gives that destination, “inside the prison.”
起 here means “raise” or “set in motion,” not simply “rise”; paired with 兵 (“troops”), it forms a compact expression for mobilizing troops.
裹 means “wrap,” and 着 marks the continuing state of being wrapped in or wearing something.
引 is the verb ‘bring’; resultative 出 marks something emerging as a result. The attached 了 marks the event as completed.
被 marks the passive, and 封为 means to confer a title or status. The status itself, 涿鹿亭侯, follows separately.
留 means ‘remain’; 在 introduces the location where someone or something remains, supplied separately here by 涿县.
做 means ‘serve as’ here, and attached 过 marks prior experience. 官, the role, remains separate.
听 is “hear,” and 后 marks what follows as happening afterward. Together they set the timing of the uncle’s reaction.
外出 means go out or away; 游学 combines 游 (travel) with 学 (study), describing study undertaken while away. The text does not specify how far he went.
相 functions adverbially with 问 to express a mutual or other-directed inquiry; here they come to ask each other. 相 does not mean “look at.”
有 (“have”) takes 志, a noun meaning “aspiration” or “resolve.” Together they express having an aim, rather than using 志 as a verb.
After the activity verb 饮, 之间 (“in the midst of”) frames the activity as the time during which something happens.
杀 is the verb “kill”; attached 了 marks the action as completed.
结为 means “form or become as”; 兄弟 names the resulting relationship, completing a reusable pattern for becoming a stated status.
备 is “prepare”; resultative 好 marks the prepared things as ready.
赶 is the action of driving or herding the horses; 着 marks it as ongoing and accompanying their arrival at the estate.
到 marks reaching the destination, and 了 presents that arrival as completed.
前 gives the direction ‘forward’ and 去 means ‘go’; together they form a compact directional predicate.
到 means ‘reach’; the attached 了 marks the arrival as completed in this context.
披 means to drape or wear something over oneself; 着 marks that state as continuing.
缠 means to wrap around; 着 presents the resulting wrapped state as continuing.
出 means ‘go out’ and 战 means ‘fight’; together they form a compact predicate for going into battle.
翻 means ‘turn’; 身 means ‘body’ and completes this compact action expression for turning the body over.
落 means ‘fall’ and 马 means ‘horse’; together they form a compact expression for falling from horseback.
杀 means ‘kill’; 死 functions as a result complement, specifying that the action ends in death.
迎 means ‘meet’ and 战 means ‘battle’; together they form a compact predicate for going to meet an opponent in combat.
斩 means ‘cut’ or ‘behead’; 成 is a result complement that introduces the resulting form, specified here by 两段.
第 marks 一 as ordinal, and 次 counts an occurrence; together they mean the first occurrence.
被 marks the subject as receiving the action, and 斩 is the action of beheading. 后, which follows, places this event in time.
投降 means surrender; 者 turns the action into a label for the people who do it.
其数 means “their number,” with 数 read shù as a noun. 不计 says it is not counted, yielding the idiomatic sense that the number is beyond counting.
混 conveys disorder or intermingling, and 战 is fighting; together they describe fighting in a confused mêlée.
退 is move or withdraw, and 后 gives the direction “back,” forming a movement predicate.

1.meaning_en: use sounding the gong as a signal
1.explanation_en: 以 introduces what is used, while 为号 assigns it the role of a signal. 鸣金 means sounding the gong; the construction links that action to its function.

解 means “undo,” and 开 is a result complement suggesting that something is opened or released; together 解开 describes bringing something to an end or freeing it. Here it refers to ending the siege. 了 marks the completed change.
到 is the verb “reach”; the following 了 marks the completed arrival, so they form one predicate. The destination remains outside the unit.
相 marks a reciprocal relation (“one another”) before the verb 拒 (“resist”), so the two sides are resisting each other.
分出 means to distinguish or bring out; 胜负 names the alternatives “victory or defeat.” Together, the construction means to settle which outcome applies.
杀 means fight or kill in this battle context; 到 marks 天明 as the time reached, giving the endpoint of the action.
带 means take or lead along; the attached 着 marks the accompanying state as they flee.
游荡 means wander; 无度 says the wandering has no limit or measure, describing its excessive extent.
骗 is the verb “fool”; 过 is a result complement showing the deception succeeded, and 了 marks the event as completed.
听 is the verb “hear”; 后 follows an event verb to place what follows it afterward. The object of hearing remains outside this unit.

1.meaning_en: served as; took up a role
1.explanation_en: 做 means “serve as” in this context, and 了 marks the taking up of the role as a completed event. The role itself follows outside this unit.
死 (‘to the death’) modifies 战 (‘fight’), describing fighting with life-or-death intensity; here 死 does not mean that someone dies.
带 is ‘bring’ or ‘take along’; attached 着 marks the resulting accompaniment or continuing state, so the people named after it are accompanying Liu Bei.
冲 means ‘surge’ or ‘shoot’; 天 (‘sky’) supplies the direction, forming a bound directional predicate. Here 天 keeps its full tone.
奉 (‘receive or carry out deferentially’) takes 命 (‘an order’) as its object; together, the established construction means acting under an order, without specifying more about it.
押 (‘guard or escort’) combines with 送 (‘convey’) into one predicate for transporting someone or something under guard.
奉 is a verb meaning to receive or carry out, and 命 is a noun meaning an order. Together, they describe acting in accordance with an order.
索 and 要 combine as a verb meaning to seek or demand something. Here it introduces the money being demanded; it does not include that object.
愤怒 describes anger, and 不已 means it does not stop. Together, the pattern expresses anger that continues intensely.

1.meaning_en: be written; have written on it
1.explanation_en: 写 means “write”; 着 has neutral tone here and marks the resulting written state as continuing. The words that follow specify what is written.
救 is the verb “rescue,” and 下 is a result complement showing that the person is successfully saved.
气 is the verb “be angry”; 得 introduces the degree or consequence described by what follows.
